steps.markdown: The **binomial** distribution counts successes in *n* independent yes/no trials, each with success probability *p*. Mean = n·p, variance = n·p·(1 − p).
Example: 10 fair coin flips. The expected number of heads is 5, but P(exactly 5 heads) = 252/1024 ≈ **0.25**. The single most likely outcome still happens only a quarter of the time.
The **Poisson** distribution counts events in a fixed interval when they happen independently at an average rate λ: calls per hour, typos per page, server errors per minute.
A Poisson variable has mean = variance = λ. If your counts have a variance much larger than their mean, the data is **overdispersed** and a Poisson model will be overconfident.
